title: hybrid-prefetch-coalescer-and-rotary-offset-simplifier-for-attention-path
author: Anika Mehta
description:
Motivation: reduce tail latency and improve sustained throughput for medium-length sequences (32-512 tokens) while retaining stable KV cache behavior under continuous batching. Existing prefetched-KV code warms individual KV slots aggressively which causes redundant device memory traffic for mixed sequence workloads and increases p95 latency when many concurrent streams start/stop. Additionally, the rotary/rope offset handling in our fused-attention path added per-token remap overhead that scales poorly for interleaved micro-batches.

What this PR does: introduces a hybrid prefetch coalescer and a rotary offset simplifier in the redwood attention runtime. The coalescer groups prefetched KV ranges across inflight requests and issues fewer contiguous device IOs; it is continuous-batch-aware (maintains coalescing window boundaries across batch flushes). The rotary offset simplifier replaces the per-token modular arithmetic with a compact offset remap table for commonly used sequence deltas and falls back to the old path only for rare long-offset cases. Together these reduce memory bandwidth, reduce kernel launch overhead, and produce a cleaner fast-path for fused-attention kernels.

Design notes: - Prefetch coalescer: maintain a small (configurable) coalescing buffer per execution stream that accumulates KV page ranges for up to N in-flight requests or M tokens before emitting a merged prefetch. The algorithm is heuristic-driven: prefer contiguous ranges, merge adjacent ranges if gap <= threshold (default 64 bytes), and respect max prefetch size to avoid evict thrash. The coalescer exposes metrics (coalesced_prefetch_count, merged_bytes, wasted_prefetch_bytes) for telemetry.
- Rotary offset simplifier: build a remap table keyed by (rotary_base_mod, requested_offset) with an LRU-style warm path. For offsets seen in the last L requests, remap is O(1) and avoids integer division/mod; for misses we compute remap and insert into the table. Table size defaults to 2048 entries per device-context and is shardable across worker threads.
- KV slot compaction: small change to the lazy-KV eviction policy to favor contiguous freed ranges to increase mergeability.
- Fallbacks: behavior remains identical to previous release (bit-for-bit on outputs) except for perf-internal ordering differences; correctness tests validate outputs identical to previous kernels for the fast-path.

Files changed (high level): runtime/attn/prefetch_coalescer.cc/h, runtime/attn/rotary_remap_table.cc/h, runtime/attn/hybrid_attn_dispatcher.cc, runtime/attn/tests/prefetch_coalescer_test.cc, kernels/fused_attn_launch.cu (fast-path hooks), infra/metrics/registry.yaml (new metrics), docs/perf/rotary-prefetch.md, bench/compare/pipelines/seq_bench.toml and a small update to CI to run the new microbench harness.

Benchmarks: microbench on A100-80GB and T4 (single-GPU), mixed workload (uniform mix of seq lengths 32/64/128/256), continuous-batch mode enabled. Numbers below are median of 5 runs.
- A100 (32 batch, concurrency 16): throughput +18% tokens/s, p50 latency -10%, p95 latency -9%.
- A100 (dynamic batching, concurrency 64): throughput +22% tokens/s, p95 latency -11%.
- T4 (small memory): throughput +11% tokens/s, p95 latency -7%, observed 12% reduction in DRAM bandwidth for KV loads.
Memory: average extra remap table memory ~12KB per stream; coalescer buffer ~64KB worst-case.

Testing: unit tests for remap table and coalescer (deterministic seeding), integration tests that compare outputs against baseline fused-attention for 200 random seeds, and end-to-end bench harness that validates stability under 10k synthetic requests. CI updated to include perf-run stage for PRs labeled with perf.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.attn.hybrid_prefetch.enabled=false by default on main; enable in canary fleets for 48h under controlled traffic. Metrics and alerting dashboards created: pref_coalesce_ratio, remap_hit_rate, avg_prefetch_bytes. If remap_hit_rate < 60% or pref_coalesce_ratio < 1.1 we automatically flip flag off for that fleet.

Related: ENG-1724 defines the continuous-batching use-cases and microbench harness, ENG-1740 requested bandwidth savings for Dedicated customers.

Notes on correctness: end-to-end model output unit tests are bit-identical for all tested model families (OPT, Llama-variants) for sequences < 1024 tokens; long sequence QA tests run with fallback path exercised.

Development checklist: - [x] Implementation - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Microbench harness - [x] Docs - [x] Perf dash + alerts - [x] Feature flag gate

Merge outcome: merged to main via squash.

review_conversation:
Evan Cho: Can you explain the eviction policy change risk for Dedicated customers?
Anika: The change biases eviction toward contiguous free regions; it does not force different end-to-end eviction schedules, only the tie-breaker. We added unit tests and a canary with KV integrity checks.
Diego Alvarez: Microbench numbers look promising. Did you test with long-running steady-state traffic?
Anika: yes — 72h stability run on canary (internal) showed no regressions and stable remap hit-rate ~92%.
Priya Reddy: Falling back on misses is a potential perf cliff. How often do misses occur?
Anika: Misses are <8% in our mixed workloads; we also log misses as a trace event for offline analysis.
Evan Cho: approve after small doc wording fix.
Anika: fixed the docs and updated the metric names per feedback.
benchmarks_summary: A100: +18-22% tokens/s for mixed seq; p95 -9 to -11%. T4: +11% tokens/s; p95 -7%. DRAM bandwidth for KV loads reduced up to 12% in representative traces. Remap hit rate median 92% under production-like mixes.
release_notes: Introduce hybrid prefetch coalescer and rotary offset remap table to improve attention throughput and tail latency. Feature behind runtime flag; opt-in via canary. Metrics added: pref_coalesce_ratio, remap_hit_rate.
notes: This PR focuses on runtime perf and is safe for fast rollout. Observability hooks added to detect regressions early. If issues occur, flip runtime.attn.hybrid_prefetch.enabled to false for the affected fleet.
